text.text_excerpt: I had been to Criollo about 1 1/2 years ago and thoroughly enjoyed it. I've been meaning to go back ever since and finally did tonight with a friend for the $35 Coolinary Dinner--I'm happy we did. Without planning it, our selections in all three courses didn't match so we covered the entire range of options. Trust me, there are no misses here. I had the Chilled crawfish lasagna with charred corn & Heirloom Spinach Sauces. It looked small but was a perfectly sized portion full of fresh crawfish and a tasty sauce. I followed with the Cabernet Braised Short Rib with Smoked Bacon & Eggplant Risotto, Red Wine Reduction. Simply delicious, I don't think I left a single grain of rice on the plate...

Criollo Restaurant & Lounge is located inside the Hotel Moteleone. If you didn't know any better, that may make the restaurant difficult to find, so to help you out if you intend to dine there, once you enter the hotel, go to the right and you will see it. I was very captivated by the ambiance of the restaurant. A lot of dark browns and woods were used in decorating this restaurant but that is offset by white walls and huge windows lining the restaurant. Despite the dark colors, it was still bright and since I do not like a poorly lit restaurant that was a huge plus for me. But, what I really liked about my experience at Criollo, is our waiter. He was funny yet professional and as attenti...

I just had the pleasure of having lunch at Criollo in the Hotel Monteleone, just in time to take advantage of their Coolinary offering! The Hotel Montleone offers garage parking for $3 after validating your ticket. The atmosphere at Ciollo is bright and pretty, without feeling too stuff. We were seated by the window facing Iberville Street (which I requested). The hotel did some pretty landscaping not ony right outside of the window, but also on the Walgreen's balcony. It was really pretty on a beautiful New Orleans day. Our waitress Kaylan was nice and attentive and really personable. I had no complaints at all. We were brought out a bread basket of 2 types of bread...regular pistolettes...
